summary: Polk Co., OR: CCC-era 100-ft tower (1939) fell in a 1942 gale; a 40-ft tower finished 1957 was destroyed by the Columbus Day Storm on Oct 12, 1962.

facts.design: 100-foot timber tower built 1939 by Arboretum camp enrollees; rebuilt in 1944; 40-foot tower with 14x14 cabin completed 1957
facts.status_note: Destroyed by the Columbus Day Storm on October 12, 1962. An NGS data sheet with 1972 marks describes concrete posts that were legs of the old tower foundation; no source says what survives today

staffing.status: Manned by a husband and wife in 1942; no later staffing found in sources read

events.note: 100-foot timber tower erected by enrollees of the Cold Springs side camp of the Arboretum camp; CCC built the access road, a combined garage, tool house and woodshed, and largely completed the cabin the same year
Polk County Fire association posted lookouts at Fanno Mountain, a new post that year (July 4, 1940)
The Hayes named as first permanent occupants (Daily Capital Journal, July 2, 1941)
Trash fire set by a Valsetz school teacher ran up the hillside toward the tower; a Dallas crew answered the alarm and fought it (per a 2005 letter)
Activated as an Aircraft Warning Service observation post on June 26, 1942
A gale of at least 90 mph on November 14, 1942 shattered the 100-foot tower; the cabin at its foot was undamaged
Construction started on a new 100-foot tower (Forest Log, June 1944)
Old tower cabin removed; concrete footings poured for new tower legs
Destroyed by the heavy winds of the Columbus Day Storm, October 12
District traded the Fanno Lookout property to Willamette Valley Lumber Company for a sub-headquarters site at Philomath
Registered November 8, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 30.5 m (100 ft) fits the 1939 tower and the 1944 rebuild. The last tower the annual reports describe on the site, a 40-foot tower with a 14x14 cabin finished in 1957, was the one standing when the lookout was destroyed in 1962.

resolved_conflicts.field: first tower: date, height and fate
resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and the Fire Lookout page say a 99-ft L-6 pole tower stood in the 1930s, replaced in 1940 by a 50-ft L-4 pole tower, both destroyed in 1962. The Forest Lookouts page quotes 1939-1944 newspapers and annual reports describing a 100-ft timber tower built in 1939 that a gale brought down in November 1942. The story follows the contemporary reports. All three sources agree on the 1962 destruction.

notes_for_editor: Brief record height 30.5 m only fits the 100-ft towers; the final tower was 40 ft (corrected). FFLOS/Fire Lookout early-tower account conflicts with the Forest Lookouts newspaper and annual-report account; story reports the contemporary account and says so. The NGS data sheet (marks stamped FANNO 1972) describes reference marks cemented in concrete posts that were legs of the old tower foundation; whether any of it survives today is unverified, and no source says what remains today. The 1964 transfer to Willamette Valley Lumber Co. is the lead for current ownership and access; not verified. No photos added: the FFLOS 1941 photo has no licence we could confirm.
